name: ST7735S 1.8" 128x160 colour TFT
description: Sitronix ST7735S driver with a 1.8-inch 128×160-pixel colour TFT (65K colours, RGB565) on a 4-wire SPI bus (write-only, up to about 15 MHz). The board has no regulator: its VCC pin feeds the chip's VDD and VDDI directly, so power it from 3.3 V. Sold as: Waveshare 1.8inch LCD Module (ST7735S, 128×160, 8-pin header VCC, GND, DIN, CLK, CS, DC, RST, BL, plus the same signals on a PH2.0 cable socket).
eli5: A small colour screen you can draw text, shapes and pictures on.

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Supply, 3.3 V (goes straight to the ST7735S VDD/VDDI, no regulator)

pins.name: DIN
pins.description: SPI data in (MOSI, the chip's SDA)

pins.name: DC
pins.description: Data/command select: low = command, high = data (the chip's A0 / D/CX)

pins.name: BL
pins.description: Backlight: high or unconnected = on (10 kΩ pull-up and transistor on the board), low = off; PWM to dim

supplierQuery: 1.8 inch TFT LCD module ST7735S 128x160 SPI
buildNotes: Power VCC from 3.3 V. The vendor page says 3.3 V/5 V, but the schematic has no regulator and the ST7735S I/O supply (VDDI) is rated to 3.7 V at most.
Init order from the datasheet: hardware reset (RST low ≥ 10 µs, then wait 120 ms), SWRESET 0x01 + 120 ms, SLPOUT 0x11 + 120 ms, COLMOD 0x3A = 0x05 (16-bit), MADCTL 0x36, DISPON 0x29.
The ST7735S RAM is 132×162 but the glass is 128×160: on this module the picture starts at RAM column 2, row 1 (portrait). Without the offset you get a stripe of random pixels along two edges.
Pixels are RGB565 sent high byte first. MicroPython's framebuf.RGB565 stores the low byte first, so swap the colour bytes before drawing into a framebuf.
SPI mode 0, write-only (no MISO). 10 MHz is safe on breadboard wires; the datasheet minimum write clock period is 66 ns (about 15 MHz).
Leave BL unconnected for a permanently lit backlight, or drive it with PWM to dim it.

driver.code:
# ST7735S 1.8" 128x160 colour TFT (Waveshare 1.8inch LCD Module), MicroPython driver.
# Written from the Sitronix ST7735S V1.1 datasheet: 4-wire SPI (mode 0), D/C low = command,
# 16-bit RGB565 pixels (COLMOD 0x3A = 0x05), sent most-significant byte first.
# The panel is 128x160 but the ST7735S RAM is 132x162, so on this module the visible area
# starts at RAM column 2, row 1 (portrait). In landscape the two offsets swap.
from machine import Pin
import framebuf
import time

BLACK = 0x0000
WHITE = 0xFFFF
RED = 0xF800
GREEN = 0x07E0
BLUE = 0x001F
YELLOW = 0xFFE0


def rgb(r, g, b):
    """24-bit colour -> RGB565."""
    return ((r & 0xF8) << 8) | ((g & 0xFC) << 3) | (b >> 3)


class ST7735:
    def __init__(self, spi, dc, cs, rst=None, landscape=False, xoff=2, yoff=1):
        self.spi = spi
        self.dc = Pin(dc, Pin.OUT, value=1)
        self.cs = Pin(cs, Pin.OUT, value=1)
        self.rst = Pin(rst, Pin.OUT, value=1) if rst is not None else None
        if landscape:
            self.width, self.height = 160, 128
            self.xoff, self.yoff = yoff, xoff
            madctl = 0x60  # MV (row/column exchange) + MX
        else:
            self.width, self.height = 128, 160
            self.xoff, self.yoff = xoff, yoff
            madctl = 0x00  # MY=MX=MV=0, RGB order
        if self.rst:
            # RESX low >= 10 us resets the chip; wait 120 ms before Sleep Out (datasheet 9.15).
            self.rst(0)
            time.sleep_ms(10)
            self.rst(1)
            time.sleep_ms(120)
        self._cmd(0x01)  # SWRESET: wait 120 ms before the next command
        time.sleep_ms(150)
        self._cmd(0x11)  # SLPOUT: booster and oscillator start, wait 120 ms
        time.sleep_ms(120)
        self._cmd(0xB1, b'\x01\x2C\x2D')  # FRMCTR1 frame rate (normal mode)
        self._cmd(0xB2, b'\x01\x2C\x2D')  # FRMCTR2 (idle mode)
        self._cmd(0xB3, b'\x01\x2C\x2D\x01\x2C\x2D')  # FRMCTR3 (partial mode)
        self._cmd(0xB4, b'\x07')  # INVCTR: column inversion
        self._cmd(0xC0, b'\xA2\x02\x84')  # PWCTR1: AVDD 5.0 V, GVDD 4.6 V, AUTO mode
        self._cmd(0xC1, b'\xC5')  # PWCTR2: VGH/VGL
        self._cmd(0xC2, b'\x0A\x00')  # PWCTR3 (normal mode)
        self._cmd(0xC3, b'\x8A\x2A')  # PWCTR4 (idle mode)
        self._cmd(0xC4, b'\x8A\xEE')  # PWCTR5 (partial mode)
        self._cmd(0xC5, b'\x0E')  # VMCTR1: VCOM
        self._cmd(0xE0, b'\x0F\x1A\x0F\x18\x2F\x28\x20\x22\x1F\x1B\x23\x37\x00\x07\x02\x10')  # gamma +
        self._cmd(0xE1, b'\x0F\x1B\x0F\x17\x33\x2C\x29\x2E\x30\x30\x39\x3F\x00\x07\x03\x10')  # gamma -
        self._cmd(0x3A, b'\x05')  # COLMOD: 16 bits per pixel
        self._cmd(0x36, bytes([madctl]))  # MADCTL: scan direction / orientation
        self._cmd(0x13)  # NORON: normal display mode
        self.fill(BLACK)
        self._cmd(0x29)  # DISPON
        time.sleep_ms(10)

    def _cmd(self, c, data=b''):
        self.cs(0)
        self.dc(0)
        self.spi.write(bytes([c]))
        if data:
            self.dc(1)
            self.spi.write(data)
        self.cs(1)

    def _window(self, x, y, w, h):
        x0, y0 = x + self.xoff, y + self.yoff
        x1, y1 = x0 + w - 1, y0 + h - 1
        self._cmd(0x2A, bytes([x0 >> 8, x0 & 255, x1 >> 8, x1 & 255]))  # CASET
        self._cmd(0x2B, bytes([y0 >> 8, y0 & 255, y1 >> 8, y1 & 255]))  # RASET

    def blit(self, buf, x, y, w, h):
        """Write w*h big-endian RGB565 pixels (2 bytes each) at (x, y)."""
        self._window(x, y, w, h)
        self._cmd(0x2C, buf)  # RAMWR

    def fill_rect(self, x, y, w, h, colour):
        x, y = max(0, x), max(0, y)
        w, h = min(w, self.width - x), min(h, self.height - y)
        if w <= 0 or h <= 0:
            return
        self._window(x, y, w, h)
        line = bytes([colour >> 8, colour & 255]) * w
        self.cs(0)
        self.dc(0)
        self.spi.write(b'\x2C')
        self.dc(1)
        for _ in range(h):
            self.spi.write(line)
        self.cs(1)

    def fill(self, colour):
        self.fill_rect(0, 0, self.width, self.height, colour)

    def pixel(self, x, y, colour):
        self.fill_rect(x, y, 1, 1, colour)

    def text(self, s, x, y, colour=WHITE, bg=BLACK):
        """Draw text with MicroPython's built-in 8x8 font."""
        w = 8 * len(s)
        buf = bytearray(w * 8 * 2)
        fb = framebuf.FrameBuffer(buf, w, 8, framebuf.RGB565)
        # framebuf stores RGB565 little-endian; the ST7735 wants the high byte first, so swap.
        sw = lambda c: ((c & 0xFF) << 8) | (c >> 8)
        fb.fill(sw(bg))
        fb.text(s, 0, 0, sw(colour))
        self.blit(buf, x, y, w, 8)

    def display(self, on=True):
        self._cmd(0x29 if on else 0x28)  # DISPON / DISPOFF

example.code:
from machine import Pin, SPI
import sys
import time
from st7735 import ST7735, WHITE, YELLOW

# Pico: GP18/GP19 belong to SPI0. ESP32: any pins work on SPI(2).
spi_id = 0 if sys.platform == 'rp2' else 2
spi = SPI(spi_id, baudrate=10000000, polarity=0, phase=0, sck=Pin({CLK}), mosi=Pin({DIN}))
tft = ST7735(spi, dc={DC}, cs={CS}, rst={RST})
time.sleep(1)
tft.text('SPARKBENCH', 24, 40, YELLOW)
tft.text('ST7735 OK', 28, 60, WHITE)
print('drawn')
while True:
    time.sleep(1)
